title: Commercialization model changed: B2B paid, personal use free (supersedes MS Store Convenience Edition)
description:
Operator directive 2026-08-06: 'we will still build the public version and commercialize it at b2b level, keeping personal use free.'

This supersedes the payments decision recorded on vanish-uninstaller-22n and adrs/0001-stack-override.md (MS Store paid Convenience Edition, decided 2026-07-11). The consequences are not cosmetic:

- Quality bar rises sharply. Every defect in epic vanish-uninstaller-7oo is a B2B dealbreaker; a paying business will not tolerate 'buttons that show but do not work.'
- Licensing/enforcement was explicitly deferred post-MVP in research.md. A B2B model needs an actual answer eventually (per-seat? site? honor-system with a commercial license file?).
- Free-for-personal + paid-for-business changes the signing/distribution calculus recorded in TASK-21 (vanish-uninstaller-1w0) and the reversal condition on 22n.
- Open-source posture (MIT today) needs re-examination against a paid B2B tier - the roadmap's own Open Source & License Assessment section discussed dual-licensing/open-core as alternatives; that discussion is now live again rather than settled.

Needs: an ADR superseding the payments half of 0001, and an updated note on 22n. Not urgent relative to the epic, but must not be silently left contradicting the docs.
acceptance_criteria: A new ADR records the B2B-paid/personal-free decision and explicitly supersedes the payments portion of adrs/0001-stack-override.md. vanish-uninstaller-22n carries a note pointing at it. The roadmap's monetization section reflects the change rather than still recommending MS Store Convenience Edition.
close_reason: ADR 0002 written and accepted: personal use free, commercial use paid, superseding only the payments row of ADR 0001. ADR 0001 marked at both the header and the row. Roadmap monetization section records model 3 as chosen with 1 superseded and 2 rejected, and says why. 22n carries a note; 1w0 carries a re-scope note (signing mandatory, Store submission now an open question). Deliberately NOT decided, and recorded as such in the ADR: price, per-seat vs site, licence-key enforcement, and the repository licence text.

title: System overview: full-width layout, and it shows no storage information
description:
Operator, 2026-08-06: 'system overview should span across the screen. no storage.'

Two defects: (a) the panel does not use the available width - it is laid out in a narrow column on a wide window, (b) storage/disk information is absent entirely despite get-system-diagnostics already returning a disks array (see scanner.ps1 Get-SystemDiagnostics and the stub fixture's shape, which includes disks: []).

For a disk-cleanup-adjacent product, per-volume capacity/free space is arguably the single most relevant system fact and it is missing.
acceptance_criteria: System overview spans the full content width at the app's default window size and reflows sensibly when narrower. Per-volume storage (capacity, free, used) renders from the real Get-SystemDiagnostics disks payload. Verified visually against the real app, not a fixture.
close_reason: Get-SystemDiagnostics asked Win32_LogicalDisk for DriveLetter, a Win32_Volume property. The query was invalid ('Invalid query'), the catch swallowed it and Storage rendered 'No local drives found' on every machine since it shipped - it never worked once. Now -ClassName/-Filter with DeviceID; a query failure surfaces instead of rendering as an empty result. Full-width was already correct and is now asserted. Verified: 2 of 2 fixed drives render.

title: App list: add a Windows Features (optional features) toggle
description:
Operator, 2026-08-06: 'all programs should have a toggle to see whether windows features should be shown or not, the ones we enable and disable from the hidden menu.'

Refers to Windows optional features - the 'Turn Windows features on or off' control panel (optionalfeatures.exe), backed by DISM /Online /Get-Features or Get-WindowsOptionalFeature. These are neither desktop apps nor Store apps, so they are currently invisible to Vanish entirely.

Scope: a toggle alongside the existing All/Desktop/Windows Apps filter that includes/excludes optional features in the list. Read-only listing first (enabled/disabled state, name, description). Enable/disable is a genuinely destructive OS-level action - if offered at all it needs Full Mode plus the mandatory-review-gate treatment, and should probably be deferred to a follow-up rather than shipped with the listing.
acceptance_criteria: A toggle shows/hides Windows optional features in the app list, defaulting to hidden. Listed entries show real enabled/disabled state from Get-WindowsOptionalFeature. The toggle's state is visible in the filter-status caption alongside the other filters. Enable/disable actions either absent or behind Full Mode + explicit review gate.
close_reason: Windows optional features now listed behind their own toggle, defaulting to hidden, with the count in the caption. Uses Win32_OptionalFeature rather than Get-WindowsOptionalFeature because the DISM cmdlet requires elevation and would make the list unavailable in Audit Mode - the CIM class returns the same 135 features unelevated in ~1s. Real Enabled/Disabled state per entry. Enable/disable deliberately not offered: the button reads 'Managed by Windows' and names optionalfeatures.exe. Verified on the real machine, 135/135.

title: Redundant software detection counts same-family entries as duplicate installations
description:
Operator, 2026-08-06: 'redundant software notifications doesnt consider that both of those entries are from the same software family, not duplicate installations.'

Concrete case from this machine: Microsoft Edge + Microsoft Edge Update (+ Edge WebView2 Runtime) are one product's components, not three competing browsers. Same applies to any updater/runtime/helper entry shipped alongside its parent app. Current detection (Get-SoftwareRedundancy) matches on category tags and flags family members as redundant with each other.

Needs family/parent grouping before redundancy comparison: entries sharing a publisher AND a name-stem (or an explicit parent relationship) are one product. Only genuinely competing products from different vendors are redundancy candidates.
acceptance_criteria: Edge + Edge Update + Edge WebView2 produce zero redundancy warnings. Two genuinely competing products (e.g. two different vendors' PDF readers) still do. Verified against the real 163-app list, where the operator confirmed almost no true duplicates exist - a correct implementation should be near-silent on this machine.
close_reason: Fixed together - all three were the same root cause. Inventory now classifies every uninstall entry (application/component/update) with a stated reason instead of dropping 60 of 151. Force Uninstall reads the same classified inventory rather than a second sweep that reapplied the old drops. Redundancy groups by product family keyed on vendor. Verified on the operator's real machine: 77 applications / 73 components / 1 update, Edge+Office+OneDrive+VSCode+WSL all ordinary applications, 1 protected entry with a reason, 0 false-positive broken entries, detection proven with a planted HKCU entry, 4 real redundancy groups down from 6. npm test 312/0.

title: System Clean: full rescan on every interaction, no incremental update, premature partial counts
description:
Operator, 2026-08-06: 'system clean rescans every time it is interacted with, not updating the previous view as per changes. this is friction as waiting time, even if 1 issue is showing but it is still scanning.'

Three defects: (a) every interaction triggers a full rescan instead of updating the existing view for the change that just happened, (b) no result caching between interactions, (c) counts render while a scan is still in flight, so the user sees a partial number presented as if final.

Relates to vanish-uninstaller-6g2 (no scan progress anywhere) - the 'is it done or is that the real number' ambiguity is the same root problem. Consider resolving together: a scan needs a definite in-progress vs complete state, and a completed scan's results need to persist across interactions with them.
acceptance_criteria: Purging/acting on one finding updates that finding's row in place without a full rescan. Scan results persist across interactions until explicitly refreshed. A count is never displayed as final while its scan is still running - in-progress state is visually distinct. Verified on the real machine where scans genuinely take seconds, not against instant fixtures.
close_reason: Root cause of the waiting was a performance bug, not just missing feedback: Open-RegistryView called OpenBaseKey on every value lookup, so the context-menu sweep never finished inside 5 minutes. Base keys are now cached per hive+view: 300s+ -> 0.7s measured on the operator's machine. Plus real progress plumbing (scanner.ps1 -> stderr marker -> main.js -> scan-progress channel -> renderer ticker), in-place row updates after purge instead of a full rescan, counts marked 'scanning' until final, selection persisted across re-renders, and re-entrancy guard. Also fixed two null-finding crashes invisible to fixtures. Verified on the real machine: 'File associations (Registry32) - step 6250 of 6465 - 294 found so far - 6s'. npm test 314/0.

title: Orphaned entries (startup items, cleaner findings) shown but not genuinely actionable
description:
Operator, 2026-08-06, two related reports: 'startup items being shown as orphaned are not addressable, no suggestions' and 'orphaned entries shown but not actionable in the true sense, even if the buttons show.'

The app surfaces findings whose action buttons render but whose action does not truly resolve the finding. This is worse than not showing the button at all - it teaches the user the app is decorative. Two sub-cases: (a) Stage 2 startup items are detection-only by design (roadmap says so) but the UI does not say so and offers no next step; (b) cleaner/orphan findings elsewhere show enabled buttons that do not fully resolve.

Per Rule 24: if something is informational-only, it must SAY so plainly and suggest what the user can do instead (e.g. 'manage this in Task Manager > Startup'). If a button is shown, it must work.
acceptance_criteria: Every finding in the app is in exactly one of two states, and says which: actionable (button present, action verifiably resolves the finding and the finding disappears on rescan) or informational (no action button, explicit text saying why, plus a concrete suggested next step). No enabled button anywhere fails to resolve what it claims.
close_reason: Two of the three reported orphans were false positives from broken exe-path extraction (scheduled-task Execute values arrive already quoted; the registry/service regex could not match unquoted paths with spaces). All three sources now share one resolver. The orphan count was also null whenever exactly one item matched, hiding the badge. Actionability resolved per Rule 24's informational branch: the panel states plainly that it only reports, and every orphaned row names the concrete place its kind of entry is managed. Genuine in-app disable/remove filed as 7oo.11. Verified on the real machine: 1 real orphan (was 3), badge visible, suggestion present and specific.

title: App list: active search/type filter was invisible (reproduced the '2 apps' report)
description:
Operator report 2026-08-06: 'total number of apps not reflected correctly, only Edge and Edge Update showing up' on both the real machine and Sandbox, despite the dashboard stat correctly showing 163/163.

Root-caused via live diagnostic, not assumed: reproduced exactly by scripting a keystroke into the search bar WHILE the real (slow, 12-18s+ observed) initial app load was still in flight. filterText was set immediately by the input handler regardless of load state; once loadApplications() finally resolved, filterAndRenderApps() correctly applied that filter, rendering exactly the apps matching 'edge' (2 of 163) - Microsoft Edge + Microsoft Edge Update/WebView2. No data bug, no rendering-count bug - the search/filter logic was always correct. The actual defect: nothing on screen indicated a filter was active, so a filter typed during the multi-second load window (or just forgotten about later) looked identical to 'the app only found 2 apps.'

Fixed: added a persistent filter-status caption under the search box (index.html/index.css .filter-status-caption, absolutely positioned so it adds zero layout height) showing 'Showing all N applications' by default or 'Showing X of N applications' + a Clear button when filterText/filterType diverge from default. Wired in renderer.js updateFilterStatus(), called from filterAndRenderApps() and at the start of loadApplications() (shows 'Loading applications...' during the load window itself).

Caught and fixed a self-inflicted regression while building this: the first version added the status as a normal flex row, which pushed the whole layout down ~33px and clipped the Start Uninstall button (fixed near the bottom of the details sidebar) 8px past the window's bottom edge - caught immediately by the existing ui-interaction-full-verify.js hit-test suite. Final version uses absolute positioning specifically to avoid taking any layout space.

Did NOT touch the underlying load-time race itself (search bar stays enabled during the multi-second load) - that's a bigger, riskier change; making an active filter impossible to miss was the safer fix that directly addresses what was actually confusing.
acceptance_criteria: filter-status-row/caption shows 'Showing all N applications' by default, 'Loading applications...' during the initial load, and 'Showing X of N applications' plus a visible Clear button whenever filterText or filterType diverge from default. Clicking Clear resets both the internal filter state and the visible search box value. Regression-tested (test/ui-interaction-verify.js) for default/filtered/cleared states. No layout regression on the details-sidebar Start Uninstall button (test/ui-interaction-full-verify.js hit-test).
close_reason: Fixed and verified 2026-08-06 (commit 2dfd10b): reproduced live (typing into search during the real load race left filterText set silently), added the always-visible filter-status caption + Clear button, absolutely positioned to avoid the layout regression the first attempt introduced (caught by ui-interaction-full-verify.js). 10 new regression assertions added. 312/312 passing.

title: No intermediate progress during long scans (leftover scan, cleaner scan, findBrokenEntries, Unlocker)
description:
Found running the real app 2026-08-05: every scan-type operation (uninstall wizard leftover scan, System Clean cleaner scans, Force Uninstall's findBrokenEntries, the Unlocker's listLockers) shows a spinner + static text with zero intermediate feedback while the underlying PowerShell can genuinely run long on a real messy machine (Advanced depth mode especially).

Root cause confirmed by code read: the ONLY streaming IPC channel in the entire app is queue-update (main.js line ~80, preload.js line ~60), used exclusively by the bulk uninstall queue panel. Every scan-type call (scanLeftovers, cleanerScan, findBrokenEntries, listLockers) is a plain ipcMain.handle request/response that blocks until the PowerShell process fully completes and returns everything in one shot - there is no plumbing for scanner.ps1 to report interim state at all.

Two options, not mutually exclusive:
1. Cheap, real now: a client-side elapsed-time counter on the loader-substatus text ('Still scanning - 14s. Advanced mode can take a while on drives with many programs.') during any scan wait. No backend change, no unmeasured performance claim (Rule 9 - it's a live clock, not a percentage), removes the 'looks frozen' perception cheaply. Needs a small reusable start/stop timer helper so it does not get duplicated across the 4+ call sites, each with its own test coverage.
2. Real streaming progress: scanner.ps1 writes periodic progress lines to stdout during a scan (e.g. every N items or every second), main.js parses and forwards via a new ipcMain->webContents.send channel mirroring the existing queue-update pattern, renderer shows a real count/percentage. Bigger, needs its own design pass on what a meaningful progress unit even is for a keyword/registry scan (item count is honest, percentage is not since total isn't known upfront).
acceptance_criteria: At minimum: every scan-type wait screen shows a live elapsed-time indicator that updates without a backend change, verified by a UI-interaction test that queues a deliberately delayed scanLeftovers response and asserts the substatus text changes over time. Stretch: a real progress channel exists and is wired into at least the leftover scan.
close_reason: Root cause of the waiting was a performance bug, not just missing feedback: Open-RegistryView called OpenBaseKey on every value lookup, so the context-menu sweep never finished inside 5 minutes. Base keys are now cached per hive+view: 300s+ -> 0.7s measured on the operator's machine. Plus real progress plumbing (scanner.ps1 -> stderr marker -> main.js -> scan-progress channel -> renderer ticker), in-place row updates after purge instead of a full rescan, counts marked 'scanning' until final, selection persisted across re-renders, and re-entrancy guard. Also fixed two null-finding crashes invisible to fixtures. Verified on the real machine: 'File associations (Registry32) - step 6250 of 6465 - 294 found so far - 6s'. npm test 314/0.

title: Startup elevation toggle: 'Start Vanish as administrator' setting (REQ-04 extension)
description:
Operator request 2026-08-03: "start as administrator for our usecase, allow for
a toggle in settings to choose the initial permission level."

WHAT THIS IS: an opt-in startup convenience. Vanish still defaults to Audit
Mode on every machine that hasn't changed the setting (safe by default,
unchanged from today). An operator who flips Settings > "Start Vanish as
administrator" gets main.js requesting elevation automatically at the next
launch, before any window is created, instead of needing a manual click on the
FLOW-01 offer.

WHAT THIS IS NOT, explicitly: a UAC bypass. Windows' own consent prompt still
appears on every single launch when the setting is on - that is by design and
this project does not attempt to route around it (promptgate Rule 13, and the
whole point of UAC). The setting only changes WHO asks Windows for elevation
(Vanish, automatically) and WHEN (before the window exists), not whether
Windows asks. No new privilege is granted: relaunch-elevated has always been
reachable from the renderer unconditionally, so this changes ordering, not
attack surface.

IMPLEMENTATION
- lib/store.js: new startupMode setting ('audit' default | 'full'), validated
  with the same schema-rule-5 fallback pattern as defaultScanMode.
- main.js: extracted attemptElevatedRelaunch(trigger) shared by the existing
  FLOW-01 manual offer/banner and the new automatic startup path, so the
  relaunch plumbing and Rule 3 (never crash on decline) live in one place.
  The automatic path runs after check-admin resolves the real tier and before
  createWindow() - if elevation succeeds, this process quits with no window
  ever shown; if declined/cancelled/unreachable, it falls through to normal
  Audit Mode exactly as today.
- index.html / renderer.js: new Settings > Startup toggle, deliberately NOT
  gated on isAdmin (unlike the autoPurge toggle below it) - the operator who
  needs this is, by definition, usually not elevated yet.

A REAL HAZARD FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING THIS: three test files
(tier-verify.js, vault-ipc-verify.js, phase4-ipc-verify.js) require('../main.js')
directly, running the REAL startup path against this machine's REAL, SHARED
settings.json. If startupMode were ever left 'full' from real use, every later
unattended run of those suites would attempt a live UAC prompt and hang
waiting on a human. Fixed with an explicit VANISH_DISABLE_AUTO_ELEVATE=1 env
var, set only by those three test files before requiring main.js - isFullMode()
still reflects the real WindowsPrincipal check regardless; only the automatic
relaunch attempt is skipped. Verified for real: planted startupMode:'full' in
this machine's actual test userData settings.json, ran tier-verify.js, 14/14
passed in 6.5s with no hang - then reverted the planted file.

Suite: 277 -> 290 passed / 0 failed unelevated.
acceptance_criteria: Settings > Start Vanish as administrator persists startupMode ('audit'|'full') via store.writeSettings with schema-rule-5 fallback. With startupMode='full' and the app not yet elevated, main.js requests elevation automatically before any window is created. Declining or cancelling UAC falls through to a working Audit Mode exactly as an unelevated launch always has (Rule 3) - never crashes, never exits uncleanly. Verified: settings-verify.js (default/round-trip/invalid-fallback/no cross-talk), UI hit-tests that the toggle is reachable in Audit Mode and round-trips through setSettings. NOT verified here (needs a human at UAC, parallel to vanish-uninstaller-69a): that toggling it on and relaunching actually produces an elevated instance with no window ever shown unelevated.
notes:
LIVE SANDBOX TEST, 2026-08-10, BOTH DIRECTIONS CONFIRMED PASS by the operator.
Elevate: toggle ON in Settings, relaunched, real UAC prompt appeared (UAC in default/prompting mode), accepting it worked correctly - elevated instance started before any Audit Mode window showed.
De-elevate (bd dtd, built this session because this exact gap was found live): toggle OFF while already elevated, Restart now clicked, no UAC prompt (correct), app closed and reopened genuinely in Audit Mode - confirmed on the v2 runas /trustlevel:0x20000 implementation after v1 (Shell.Application COM) failed live and was replaced same-day.
close_reason: Live sandbox test confirms both directions of the startup-elevation toggle work end to end: elevate-on-launch triggers a real UAC prompt and elevates correctly before any window shows; the new Restart now button (bd dtd) de-elevates back to Audit Mode with no prompt, as designed. See notes for the v1-failed/v2-fixed detail on the de-elevate mechanism.

title: Widen UI hit-test coverage to the main user flows
description:
Raised by the operator 2026-08-03: "a lot of these tests ignore the ui and
directly use command line to the functionality. if a user experiences a hiccup
in the uiux, they wont trust vanish anymore."

Assessment. Partly already handled, partly a real gap.

ALREADY HANDLED: test/ui-interaction-verify.js loads the real index.html with a
stubbed window.api and hit-tests with document.elementFromPoint, asserting the
topmost element at a control's centre IS that control. That is the right
technique, and the suite exists because an invisible overlay with
pointer-events:all once covered every dialog in the app (da4fd36) -- buttons
rendered perfectly and did nothing.

THE GAP: the slice is narrow. As of 2ca22f2 it covers the elevation offer,
inactive-overlay hit-testing, the confirm and typed-confirm dialogs, the SEC-1
acknowledgement dialog, the unlocker dialog, tab navigation, and Audit Mode
control locking. It does NOT cover the main flows a user actually spends their
time in:

  * the application list rendering real engine output shapes
  * the uninstall wizard across its screens
  * the leftovers tree (select-all, per-item toggles, risk grouping)
  * the Quarantine Manager restore / Delete Forever paths
  * the bulk queue panel and its risky-uninstaller acknowledgement
  * System Clean scan -> select -> purge

Nothing asserts that engine data RENDERS either: an empty list, an error
result, or a value of an unexpected shape. scanner.ps1 already coerces
REG_MULTI_SZ display fields to string because a String[] DisplayName once broke
the whole renderer list -- that regression has engine-side coverage but no UI
assertion that the list survives it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this app runs elevated and deletes things. A
control that looks armed but is inert, or a confirmation the user cannot reach,
is not a cosmetic defect here -- it is either a destructive action taken
without real consent, or a user who stops trusting the tool.

Extend ui-interaction-verify.js rather than starting a new harness; the
fixture (test/fixtures/stub-preload.js) can already queue per-call responses,
which is the seam needed to drive error and edge-case branches.
acceptance_criteria: ui-interaction-verify.js drives, and hit-tests, each of: the app list rendering real engine shapes (empty list, one app, an app with a REG_MULTI_SZ-style odd DisplayName, an error result); the uninstall wizard end to end across all screens; the leftovers tree including select-all and per-item toggles; the Quarantine Manager restore and Delete Forever paths; the queue panel including the risky-uninstaller acknowledgement; and System Clean scan-to-purge. Each asserts the control is the topmost element at its own centre, not merely visible.
close_reason: Fixed in 3123db8. Extended ui-interaction-verify.js (Audit Mode) with app-list edge cases (empty, error, REG_MULTI_SZ shape). New ui-interaction-full-verify.js (fixture-simulated Full Mode) drives the uninstall wizard end to end, leftovers tree select-all/per-item toggles, Quarantine Manager restore (incl. overwrite-conflict) and Delete Forever double-confirm, the queue panel and risky-uninstaller ack, and System Clean scan-to-purge - every assertion hit-tests the real clickable target with elementFromPoint. Fixture gained a generic per-method response-override queue. One test-authoring bug caught and fixed (not an app bug): the restore-point checkbox is a deliberately zero-size input behind a visible slider. Suite 212 -> 277 passed / 0 failed. Wired into run-all.ps1 as a new electron-full suite kind.

title: Confirm the elevated relaunch UAC branch on a spaced path (TASK-05 remainder)
description:
Remainder of vanish-uninstaller-ceb, filed rather than claimed.

The argument-quoting defect is FIXED and verified in 2989f62: every case
round-trips through CommandLineToArgvW, the real Windows parser. What that does
NOT prove is the end-to-end behaviour, because the relaunch triggers UAC and
needs a human at the consent prompt.

Needs a human to confirm, from a checkout whose path CONTAINS A SPACE (the dev
folder was renamed to D:\quickhelp, so reproduce deliberately - e.g. copy the
checkout to "C:\test folder\vanish"):

1. Launch unelevated. Accept the startup elevation offer.
   -> an elevated instance starts, the unelevated one exits, one instance total.
2. Launch unelevated. DECLINE the offer.
   -> stays in a working Audit Mode, no exit, no crash (Rule 3).
3. Launch unelevated. Accept, then CANCEL the UAC prompt.
   -> same as (2): Audit Mode, no exit, no crash.

Branches 2 and 3 were already listed as unverified in the /cso handoff. This is
the last unverified part of phase 1 and blocks REQ-05 acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: From a checkout whose path contains a space, clicking Restart as administrator launches an elevated instance, the unelevated instance exits, and only one instance remains. The decline/cancel branch lands in a working Audit Mode without exiting or crashing.
notes: Sandbox harness ready (test/sandbox/). ROOT CAUSE of 'never saw a UAC prompt' found 2026-08-04: host machine's UAC slider is at 'Never notify' (ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=0, PromptOnSecureDesktop=0) - elevation silently succeeds for this admin account on every app, no dialog ever, host-wide. Vanish's own code (scanner.ps1 relaunch-elevated: Start-Process -Verb RunAs) is correct and unaffected as a bug - Windows just doesn't ask. Accept branch is testable on host (always succeeds); decline/cancel branches are NOT testable on host at all (no dialog to decline). Sandbox should default to normal UAC behavior since it boots a separate clean image - use it for all three branches, verify this expectation holds when run.
close_reason:
PROVEN LIVE, unattended, 2026-08-28. test/sandbox/relaunch-live-probe.ps1, 12 passed 0 failed, registered in run-all.ps1.

The reason this sat open was that the elevated harness is ALREADY elevated - asking an administrator to become an administrator succeeds trivially and proves nothing - so it was believed to need a human at a consent prompt. It does not. The probe drops privilege first, then tests from below.

STAGE 1 (elevated) drops to a genuinely unprivileged token. STAGE 2 (unprivileged, asserted so - callerElevated must be false or the run proves nothing) asks the engine for relaunch-elevated targeting a marker script under a path with spaces in BOTH the directory and the filename. The marker script records the token it actually runs with. THE ASSERTION: the relaunched process reports IsInRole(Administrator) TRUE, having been launched by an unprivileged caller. Not an exit code, not the engine's own success claim - the launched process's report of itself.

Also confirmed on the same spaced path: a spaced executable path is quoted as ONE argument, a spaced ARGUMENT is quoted too (not just the executable), and a bare token is left unquoted rather than defensively wrapped.

ONE MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: the first version used runas.exe /trustlevel:0x20000 because it is the Windows-documented mechanism, and it silently did nothing - which 9vp had ALREADY MEASURED in this repository ('runas.exe /trustlevel:0x20000  NO RESULT (exit 1)') with the working answer, a scheduled task at RunLevel Limited, in the same comment. Writing against the documented mechanism instead of the measured one cost a full failing run. It is also the second time runas has been trusted here - in 0.5.0 it exited 0 while doing nothing, so the app reported a successful de-elevation and came back Full Mode.

NOT PROVEN, and it cannot be on this machine: the 'declined' branch. ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=0 auto-approves, so Win32 1223 cannot be produced at all. The mapping that would run on it is covered by test/uac-cause-verify.js.

title: SEC-3 (HIGH): data-dir ACL hardening is incomplete and its health check reports a false positive
description:
Found by /cso audit 2026-08-03 (TASK-18). FIXED in 35e02d2 -- full detail restored
now that the bug is closed (it was withheld while this public repo carried an
unfixed privilege-escalation path).

THE BUG -- three defects, one root cause.

Root cause: Vanish state lived directly in app.getPath('userData'), which is also
Chromium's profile directory. That made the hardening unfixable in place -- the
ACL that stops a standard user rewriting manifest.json (consumed by the engine as
ELEVATED instructions) is the same ACL that stops Chromium writing Preferences,
Cache and Local Storage on the next Audit Mode run.

1. Set-VanishDataDirAcl called $acl.SetOwner($admins) on the top-level directory
   only and never recursed. store.init creates the vault subdirectory on EVERY
   start including Audit Mode, and store.appendOplog writes oplog.jsonl before any
   tier gate -- so on the documented normal flow (Audit Mode start, then the
   elevation offer) those objects were created owned by the unprivileged user.
   On Windows an object's owner always retains READ_CONTROL and WRITE_DAC, so that
   user could rewrite the ACL of vault\ and manifest.json at will and hand itself
   write access back.
2. Test-VanishDataDirAcl inspected only the top directory's DACL -- never the
   Owner field, never any child. It therefore returned protected:true while the
   vault subtree was still attacker-writable.
3. main.js only re-applies the ACL when the check reports protected:false, so once
   that false positive landed, nothing ever re-checked. This was the load-bearing
   defect: the remediation could not fire.

EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED on the development host at audit time:
  %APPDATA%\vanish-uninstaller   AreAccessRulesProtected=True
    CHILD vault        owner=<interactive user>  protected=False
    CHILD oplog.jsonl  owner=<interactive user>  protected=False

Consequence: the Vuln 2 remediation did not hold on any machine where the app had
run unelevated first. Fed SEC-2 (vanish-uninstaller-2xt), which turned manifest
control into an elevated write to the all-users Startup folder.

THE FIX
State moved to a "vanish-state" subdirectory that nothing but Vanish writes, so it
can be locked without breaking Chromium in Audit Mode. Existing installs migrate
once, per item, never clobbering an already-migrated file and leaving in place
anything it could not move -- a half-finished migration must not lose a vault
payload. Ownership is reassigned across the whole subtree (cheap now that the
subtree is Vanish-only rather than the Chromium profile). Test-VanishDataDirAcl
checks owners as well as the DACL.

Regression tests: the exact false-positive condition -- protected DACL, zero
non-administrator writers, user-owned children -- is asserted in
test/security-verify.ps1 and runs in BOTH tiers, since the check has no elevation
gate. test/store-migration-verify.js covers fresh install, migration with
byte-for-byte payload integrity, and idempotency.

STILL UNVERIFIED: the recursive ownership reassignment itself (icacls /setowner)
is elevation-gated and needs an elevated run of test/run-all.ps1.
acceptance_criteria: Ownership is reassigned recursively, not just on the root; Test-VanishDataDirAcl inspects owners as well as the DACL, covers the vault subtree, and treats an unexpected owner as unprotected so main.js re-applies; a test asserts the false positive is gone.
close_reason: Fixed in 35e02d2. Root cause was the state directory being the shared Chromium profile root, making the lock unfixable in place; state moved to a vanish-state subdirectory with a once-only, non-destructive migration. Ownership now reassigned across the subtree (owner retains WRITE_DAC regardless of DACL). Test-VanishDataDirAcl now inspects owners as well as the DACL - that was the load-bearing bug, since main.js only re-applies when it reports protected:false. VERIFIED unelevated: the exact false-positive condition (protected DACL, zero non-admin writers, user-owned children) is asserted in test/security-verify.ps1 and now reports unprotected; store-migration-verify.js covers fresh/migrate/idempotent. NOT YET VERIFIED: the recursive ownership reassignment itself needs an elevated run. Suite 182 passed / 0 failed.

title: SEC-2 (HIGH): vault restore destination check is a blocklist with administrator-only gaps
description:
Found by /cso audit 2026-08-03 (TASK-18). FIXED in b50cc5c -- full detail restored
now that the bug is closed (it was withheld while this public repo carried an
unfixed privilege-escalation path).

THE BUG
Test-ProtectedDestination was the only check on where an elevated vault restore
may write, and it failed twice over.

1. Blocklist coverage. It covered %SystemRoot% (and by prefix System32, SysWOW64,
   WinSxS, INF, Boot) plus $PSScriptRoot. It did NOT cover
   C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp, per-user Startup
   folders, or direct children of a drive root.
2. Textual comparison. It compared [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath output, which
   normalises a path but does NOT follow junctions. Any check of this shape was
   bypassable regardless of coverage.

Invoke-VaultRestore called it once and then, with onConflict=overwrite, deleted
whatever sat at originalPath and moved the vault payload there. Both values came
from manifest.json, which the threat model treats as untrusted input.

EXPLOIT (coverage variant)
1. While the data directory was still user-writable (before the first elevated
   run -- see SEC-3, which is what kept it writable), write a manifest entry with
   a valid UUIDv4 id, a payload EXE inside the entry folder so Resolve-SafeVaultPath
   passes, and originalPath =
   C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp\OneDriveSync.exe
2. Operator runs Vanish elevated, opens Quarantine Manager, clicks Restore (overwrite).
3. The elevated process moves the attacker's binary into all-users Startup. It
   runs at every logon, including for administrators.

EXPLOIT (junction variant -- defeats the fix to variant 1 on its own)
1. Pre-create a directory junction at an allowed path, e.g.
   %LOCALAPPDATA%\SomeApp -> C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp
2. Set originalPath = %LOCALAPPDATA%\SomeApp\OneDriveSync.exe
3. The guard sees a LocalAppData path and allows it; the move follows the junction
   into all-users Startup.

THE FIX
Destinations are resolved before being judged: walk to the deepest existing
ancestor, follow its reparse point, re-attach the remaining segments, and check
BOTH the literal and the resolved path. Refuses any "Start Menu" subtree in any
profile, direct children of a drive root, the Windows directory, and reparse
points it cannot read.

%ProgramFiles%, %ProgramData% and other user profiles stay ALLOWED on purpose --
a correction to the audit's own recommendation. Vanish legitimately quarantines
application leftovers from all three (REQ-17 sweeps other profiles by design), so
a restore must be able to put them back; blocking them would break the undo path,
which is the point of the vault. The narrow execution-surface list is the control.

New read-only protected-destination-probe engine action makes the guard testable
in Audit Mode as well as Full Mode, since vault-restore is elevation-gated.
Regression tests cover every refusal, every must-still-work restore, and the
junction bypass with a real junction.
acceptance_criteria: A restore destination outside a permitted root is refused; the administrator-only locations enumerated in the local report (finding 2) are all rejected; test/security-verify.ps1 forges a manifest entry targeting one of them and asserts refusal.
notes: 2026-08-03 follow-up: fresh adversarial re-review of this fix found that Resolve-DestinationTarget only followed ONE hop of a junction chain. Destination guard now resolves junctions before judging (the textual comparison was the deeper bug -- it made any path blocklist bypassable), and refuses Start Menu subtrees, drive-root children and unreadable reparse points. title: Elevated relaunch fails when the repo path contains a space (TASK-05)
description:
Clicking 'Restart as administrator' (banner or startup offer) fails with:
  Error launching app / Unable to find Electron app at D:\quickhelp / Cannot find module 'D:\quickhelp'

NOT a build problem - it is argument quoting on the relaunch path.

main.js relaunch-elevated sends argList = app.isPackaged ? [] : [app.getAppPath()], which unpackaged is 'D:\quickhelp projects\vanish-uninstaller'. scanner.ps1 relaunch-elevated then calls Start-Process -FilePath $Params.exePath -ArgumentList $argList -Verb RunAs. PowerShell joins an -ArgumentList array with spaces WITHOUT quoting, so Electron gets 'D:\quickhelp' and 'projects\vanish-uninstaller' as two args and tries to open the first as the app.

Proposed fix (unverified, needs a human at the UAC prompt):
  $quoted = @($argList | ForEach-Object { '"' + $_ + '"' })
  Start-Process -FilePath $Params.exePath -ArgumentList $quoted -Verb RunAs -ErrorAction Stop
-FilePath already handles a spaced path; only -ArgumentList needs quoting.

Why it hid: only reproduces when the project path contains a space, and only on the unpackaged/dev path (packaged builds send an empty arg list, so it would appear fixed at release while the latent quoting bug remains). No automated coverage because the relaunch triggers UAC.

Blocks REQ-05 acceptance and the TASK-05 UAC branches, which were already the last unverified part of phase 1.
acceptance_criteria: From a checkout whose path contains a space, clicking Restart as administrator launches an elevated instance of Vanish (not an error dialog), the unelevated instance exits, and only one instance remains. Plus a regression test that asserts the constructed argument vector survives a spaced path without needing UAC.
notes: 2026-08-03: the dev folder was renamed D:\quickhelp projects -> D:\quickhelp to remove the space. That MASKS this bug locally - it does not fix it. The default install target is C:\Program Files\Vanish, which also contains a space, so the argument-quoting fix in main.js relaunch-elevated is still required. Do not close this on the strength of the symptom disappearing on the dev machine; reproduce by installing to a path with a space.
close_reason: Argument-quoting defect fixed in 2989f62. ConvertTo-ProcessArgument implements the real CommandLineToArgvW rules rather than the naive quote-wrapping proposed in the report, which would have broken on a trailing backslash and allowed argument injection into an elevated process. VERIFIED by round-tripping through CommandLineToArgvW itself: spaced path, trailing backslash, embedded quote, multiple spaced args, and the no-op case all come back identical. New relaunch-argv-probe exposes the vector without triggering UAC - the absence of that seam is why this shipped uncovered. End-to-end UAC confirmation filed separately as vanish-uninstaller-69a rather than claimed here. Suite 199 passed / 0 failed.

title: Vendor web fonts and icon set - drop the last runtime network calls (Rule 6 / NFR-06 / INV-4)
description:
index.html loads FontAwesome 6.4.0 from cdnjs.cloudflare.com and index.css @imports Inter+Outfit from fonts.googleapis.com. Both are outbound HTTP requests on every launch, which contradicts promptgate Rule 6, NFR-06 (zero runtime network I/O) and Codex INV-4. Found during phase 1 implementation 2026-08-03.

Mitigation already in place: index.html now carries a strict CSP with connect-src 'none' (no fetch/XHR/WebSocket possible) and the two CDN origins explicitly pinned in style-src/font-src, so the exposure is declared and cannot grow silently. It is not resolved.

Resolution options for the operator:
1. Vendor both locally (assets/ folder). FontAwesome Free licensing per Rule 11: icons CC BY 4.0 (attribution required in README/about), fonts SIL OFL 1.1, CSS MIT. Inter and Outfit are both SIL OFL 1.1. All compatible with an MIT app; attribution must be added.
2. Drop FontAwesome for a hand-authored inline SVG sprite (41 icons in use) and drop the web fonts for the existing Segoe UI fallback. Zero third-party licensing, but it is a visual restyle and 02-uiux.md says this pack extends the design system rather than restyling it - so it needs the operator's sign-off.

Recommended: option 1 (vendor + attribute) - keeps the design identity, removes the network call, cheap.
acceptance_criteria: A launch with the network adapter disabled renders identically to a launch with it enabled; no request leaves the process; CSP can be tightened to default-src 'self' with no external origins; any bundled font/icon license is recorded per Rule 11.
close_reason: Resolved by designing the assets rather than vendoring third-party ones (operator direction: 'find something free or design things yourself'). assets/icons.css is a first-party 45-glyph set on a 24x24 grid with a 2px stroke, delivered as CSS mask images so glyphs paint in currentColor and every existing <i class='fa-solid fa-x'> keeps working with zero markup changes - no FontAwesome, no licence to carry, no attribution burden. Web fonts replaced with the OS stack (Segoe UI Variable / Segoe UI), which is native on both target OS versions. CSP now names NO external origin: default-src 'self' + connect-src 'none'. Verified: app boots with zero CSP violations and zero console errors, and the icon set was visually reviewed at multiple sizes (seven glyphs redrawn after the first pass read wrong - gears looked like a sun, cubes like a molecule, rocket like an insect).

description: Phase 5. Spec: 05-implementation-plan.md TASK-19. MVP DoD-3. /code-review high + /security-review across all deletion/registry/service/elevation/queue paths; fix or written-waive.
notes:
EARLY PASS PERFORMED 2026-08-03 (task stays open: it is sequenced after TASK-17's VM pass, and should be re-run against the VM-verified build before DoD-3 is claimed).

Focused review of the destructive surfaces. Three real findings, all FIXED and regression-tested in test/security-verify.ps1 (32/32), full suite 280/280:

VULN-1 HIGH - path traversal / EoP in the quarantine vault. manifest.json is user-writable but the engine acts on it elevated. A forged entry could move an attacker file anywhere incl. System32 (originalPath), read a payload from outside the vault (traversing vaultRelative), reg-import an arbitrary .reg (traversing regFile), or recursively force-delete an arbitrary directory (traversing entryId). FIX: UUID validation on entry ids before any Join-Path; Resolve-SafeVaultPath proves containment; Test-ProtectedDestination refuses restores into the Windows directory.

VULN-2 HIGH - elevated process trusting a user-writable data directory. Closes the ASSUMED item in 01-trd.md security section. FIX: elevated start checks the ACL and applies Administrators+SYSTEM FullControl / Users ReadAndExecute with inheritance severed; result logged to oplog.

VULN-3 MEDIUM - elevated execution of attacker-plantable uninstallers. queue.json was trusted at execution time; HKCU entries can name any binary. FIX: live registry re-read at execution; Get-UninstallerTrust flags HKCU + user-writable binaries; typed acknowledgement required or the item is skipped; engine enforces independently.

Bonus bug found by the new test: the ACL checker's write mask was built from Modify|FullControl, which share read bits with ReadAndExecute, so it misreported the intended read-only Users ACE as a writer.

DEFERRED TO /cso (TASK-18): pre-existing exec(uninstallString) in the uninstall-native handler. Unchanged by this branch so out of scope for a diff review, but it is a shell-execution surface fed by a registry value and deserves the repo-wide pass.

Done as a targeted review of the destructive surfaces plus durable regression tests, which is the form that survives the session.

FINDINGS, all negative (no defects found), each verified rather than assumed:

1. Tier model holds completely. Enumerated all 34 ipcMain handlers against the 17 registered through fullModeOnly(). Every channel that mutates the machine is gated: create-restore-point, purge-remnants, uninstall-native, vault-restore, vault-delete, kill-process, unlock-path, the six queue-* channels, network-hold-apply/revert, startup-action, cleaner-purge. Every ungated channel is a read: get-*, list-*, scan-*, find-broken-entries, and the four new snapshot/attribution channels.
2. set-settings is ungated and that is correct, not an oversight. It can set startupMode='admin', but that only means the NEXT launch requests elevation, which still shows UAC - no privilege is granted by the write. The channel that actually creates the scheduled task, startup-action, IS gated.
3. The new surfaces (measure-paths, install-snapshot, attribution-scan) are read-only by construction and now by regression: 14 new assertions in test/security-verify.ps1, placed ABOVE the tier gate on purpose because Audit Mode is the tier the read-only promise is about - running them only when elevated would regress the promise exactly never.
4. Command injection through the new path-list parameter: proven handled as data with a canary. measure-paths is the first engine command to take a caller-supplied LIST rather than a single validated target, so the base64-JSON parameter boundary was re-proven for it rather than assumed to carry over.
5. Static guarantees extended: Measure-Paths is asserted to contain no Invoke-Expression/Start-Process/cmd.exe and no Remove-Item/Set-Content/Out-File/New-Item. It enumerates and reads .Length; it cannot execute or write.

SCOPE STATED HONESTLY: this is a focused review of the destructive surfaces and of everything added this cycle, not a multi-hour full-codebase /cso sweep. The prior /cso pass (2026-08-03, four issues found and fixed - command injection, a restore destination bypassable by a directory junction, an ACL fix that did not survive normal startup order, an untracked lockfile) still stands and its regressions still pass. What is new here is coverage of the surfaces that did not exist then. A future full sweep should start from the areas this did NOT re-derive: the vault restore path and the leftover scanner's path handling, both of which are covered by existing SEC-1/SEC-2/SEC-3 regressions but were not re-reviewed line by line this session.
