The blocker was assumed to be 'needs Full Mode', but the stub preload already simulates Full Mode via VANISH_STUB_TIER, and the backend gate (fullModeOnly on cleaner-purge) is proved separately by phase4-ipc-verify. Nothing had to be deleted on a real machine to prove the aggregation logic.

test/clean-all-verify.js drives cleanAllCleaners() with confirmDialog replaced by a recorder, so 'one aggregate confirmation' is MEASURED rather than asserted from reading the code:
- ONE dialog for the whole action, not one per section. Six dialogs in a row is how a user learns to click through them without reading, which would turn the Advanced-risk one into a reflex.
- The dialog counts items AND sections up front ('Clean 3 item(s) across 2 section(s)?') and breaks the total down per section, so 'clean all' is never an unnamed quantity.
- It states that everything goes to Quarantine first and can be put back.
- With an Advanced-risk item present it requires typing CLEAN, says the words 'Advanced risk', NAMES the risky items, and says what that means (it can affect software still installed). Without one there is no typed gate - a gate on every bulk action is a gate nobody reads.
- Declining purges nothing and leaves every section untouched. With nothing scanned it asks nothing and does nothing rather than confirming an empty action.
- The button carries data-destructive, so it tier-locks in Audit Mode like every other destructive control.
- A section whose only finding is list-only (removable=false) is SKIPPED, not sent as an empty purge.

That last one needed a harness improvement: the stub recorded call COUNTS but not arguments, so 'it called cleanerPurge twice' could not distinguish which two sections it sent. window.__test.callArgs(method) now records the arguments each channel was called with, structure-cloned so a later renderer mutation cannot rewrite what the test believes was sent.

title: Health Advisor System Overview cards should fit one row when maximized
description: 6 fixed system-info cards (index.html:325-331, .audit-cards-grid in index.css:1602-1614) use auto-fit minmax(200px,260px), which needs up to 1610px to hold all 6 in one row and wraps earlier than that on many maximized-window widths. Lower the minmax bounds (or add a wide-viewport breakpoint) so all 6 fit in one row at typical maximized widths while still wrapping gracefully on narrow windows. Verify no other element reuses .audit-cards-grid with a different card count before changing bounds (AGP-8 risk: layout change rippling to unrelated screen).
close_reason: Lowered .audit-cards-grid minmax from (200px,260px) to (150px,220px) - index.css:1602-1615. 6 cards now need 950-1310px of content width instead of up to 1610px to share one row, and .audit-cards-grid is used nowhere else (grepped) so this cannot ripple elsewhere (AGP-8 check done). .card-value.wrap already handles text wrapping at the narrower width. Not pixel-verified on the operator's actual maximized window (no GUI access from this session) - if a particular display is still narrow enough to wrap, the fix is the same lever (lower the bounds further), not a different approach.

title: Network attribution panel: reach a verdict, including the negative one
description: Step 1 of the revised bfh build order. A Health Advisor section that answers 'what is using my network' and can answer 'nothing here is' - the fourth outcome - with zero network I/O, so INV-4 stands untouched. Facts only: adapter throughput sampled from local byte counters, connections grouped by owning process, Wi-Fi signal, Windows Update transfer state. NOT per-process bandwidth: Windows does not attribute bytes to a process without an ETW kernel trace, and the panel must say so rather than implying a per-app rate.
design: Fast local sources only, measured before choosing: .NET NetworkInterface.GetIPStatistics for byte counters and link speed (44ms, no module load, covers v4+v6), netstat -ano for connections by PID (40ms), netsh wlan for signal (217ms), Get-DeliveryOptimizationStatus for update transfers (583ms, and only Status=Downloading counts - the 12 Caching rows on this machine are completed files, reporting them as active would be a Rule 24 false alarm). Get-NetAdapter/Get-NetTCPConnection were rejected at 2.5s and 1.3s: module autoload is paid on every call because the engine spawns a fresh powershell per action. Verdict computed in the engine as a code; the sentences live in the renderer with the rest of the copy.
acceptance_criteria: The panel states a verdict, not a connection list. With the machine quiet it says nothing here is using the network and what it examined. No string in the section claims a per-process byte rate or a percentage improvement. Zero network calls: scanner.ps1 still has no Invoke-WebRequest/WebClient/socket.
close_reason: Shipped in the network attribution commit: Get-NetworkActivity + Health Advisor section, four verdicts, zero network I/O (asserted by name in test/network-verify.ps1). npm test 361/0, npm run verify 173/0. Suppression and revert - step 2 of the bfh order - is the next piece and is not in this.

title: Stage 8 reduced: before/after install snapshot diff
description: No issue exists for the reduced Stage 8. Not the live installer-hooking engine (that was cut as the biggest lift on the roadmap): snapshot the Run-key hives and top-level Program Files/AppData listings immediately before and after a monitored install, and report the delta as one line of real numbers ('14 new registry keys, 3 new folders'). Reuses Stage 1's existing restore-point trigger. Total Rollback Purge stays deferred - build it only if the diff report proves people need more than scan+quarantine.
notes: PROMOTED 2026-08-12. Genuinely unserved: the tools that did before/after install snapshots on Windows (InstallWatch, ZSoft Uninstaller) are dead, and nothing mainstream replaced them - Windows itself offers no answer to 'what did that installer actually change'. Low effort, reuses Stage 1's existing restore-point trigger, and it FEEDS bu2's attribution: a recorded install delta is ground truth about which paths belong to which program, rather than a heuristic guess. Pairs with the cut of ag0 - 'what changed on this machine and when' is the real question behind wanting to roll updates back.
close_reason:
Shipped. Engine: Get-InstallSnapshot (scanner.ps1) reads Run hives, top-level Program Files/ProgramData/AppData directories, uninstall keys and services; read-only, so the 'install-snapshot' action is reachable in Audit Mode on purpose - 'what did that installer change' is an audit question and gating it behind elevation would give the honest answer only to users who had already granted more power.

Diff is lib/snapshot.js, pure and injected nothing: the engine takes readings, this decides what a reading MEANS. Three decisions that a naive diff gets wrong, each with an assertion: a case-only path rewrite is not a change (Windows paths are case-preserving, not case-sensitive); an unreadable category reports ZERO removals rather than 'everything was deleted', and says so in the summary; output is sorted so two identical installs read identically instead of following OS enumeration order. Additions lead the summary and removals follow, because a user watching an install does not expect to be told about deletions and reads that as an alarm.

attributionPaths() is the payload bu2 needs: added directories only (registry entries are not paths and carry no bytes), recorded to the oplog as install-snapshot-diff so a path's owner is FACT rather than heuristic.

The 'before' reading is held in the main process, not the renderer, so a reload cannot lose it, and it deliberately survives a failed second reading so the user retries instead of losing the session - the error message says so.

Verified: npm test 465/0 (was 442/0), 23 new assertions in test/snapshot-verify.js registered in run-all.ps1. Engine proven against this real machine (10 run entries, 233 dirs, 187 uninstall keys, 319 services) and a real round trip: created a folder under LOCALAPPDATA between two readings, diff reported '1 folder added' and attributed the exact path.

Layout bug caught by screenshot, not by tests: the card first reused .cleaner-section, which is a COLLAPSIBLE (overflow:hidden, body display:none until .expanded) - it clipped the card to 86px and hid the entire result. Nothing overlapped, so the hit-test suite saw nothing wrong. Now has its own always-open .snapshot-card class, 231px, verified rendering with the result list and the honest 'this is a comparison, not a recording' caveat visible.

title: Stage 11: orphaned MSI/MSP installer cache sweep (1.2GB measured)
description: Measured 1.2GB in C:\Windows\Installer on the operator's machine 2026-08-02. Only the driver-store half of Stage 11 has an issue (0ng); this half has none. Cross-reference .msi/.msp files against HKLM\...\Installer\LocalPackages to find unreferenced installers - PatchCleaner is the reference implementation for the orphan logic. Removing a referenced package breaks repair/uninstall for that product, which is why this is a NEEDS-ORPHAN-DETECTION category, never a glob delete.
acceptance_criteria: No file still referenced by an installed product is ever proposed; every removal goes to the vault first and restores.
notes: Kept, but NOT as a subsystem: this is a finding TYPE inside the cleaner surface that already exists, not a new panel. The orphan rule is a registry cross-reference against HKLM...\Installer\LocalPackages - small, public knowledge, no FOSS to integrate (PatchCleaner is closed freeware). What Vanish adds over PatchCleaner is the vault: PatchCleaner moves files to a folder and calls it a day. 1.2GB measured on the operator's machine 2026-08-02.
close_reason:
Shipped 2026-08-18 as an AUDIT-ONLY finding type inside the existing cleaner surface, which is what the notes asked for (not a new panel). Find-OrphanInstallerCache cross-references %SystemRoot%\Installer against every LocalPackage under Installer\UserData - Products AND Patches, because missing the Patches half would offer every .msp on the machine - and returns NOTHING at all if that reference scan reads nothing, since an empty reference set makes every cached installer look orphaned. Measured here: 105 cached files / 977 MB, 76 referenced, 29 orphans / 136.8 MB.

THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS NOT MET, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS AUDIT-ONLY. 'Every removal goes to the vault first and restores' is impossible for this location: the cache is under %SystemRoot%, which the restore path blocks as a destination (see z3s). Measured, not assumed - a planted orphan quarantined cleanly and the restore returned 'Rejected: refusing to restore into a protected system location' with the payload stranded. Offering the removal anyway would ship a deletion with no way back, dressed as a reversible one. The 136.8 MB stays unclaimed until the vault can honour the promise; that unlock is the open half of z3s (permit a restore to the recorded originalPath), and it is an operator security call.

25 assertions in test/dead-reference-verify.ps1, including the one the feature rests on: no file still referenced by an installed product is ever proposed (0 violations against an independently-built reference set).

title: Consume CleanerML definitions rather than writing cleaners; the vault is what makes them ours
description:
RESCOPED 2026-08-12 on operator direction. Writing our own risk-tiered cleaner catalogue was the largest item on the roadmap and would have been a worse copy of work already done and maintained by other people.

ALREADY SOLVED: the cleaner definitions themselves. BleachBit's cleanerml repo carries hundreds of maintained, per-application cleaning rules in CleanerML, an XML markup language, and has done for years. Re-deriving those rules by hand for Windows applications is exactly the redundant work we are refusing.

NOT SOLVED BY ANYONE: reversible cleaning. Every commodity cleaner - BleachBit, CCleaner, Storage Sense - deletes. Vanish's vault (INV-1: no removal without a restore path) is the one thing in this space nobody offers, and it is the reason people distrust cleaners generally. Running someone else's well-tested definitions THROUGH our quarantine-and-restore pipeline is a product nobody currently sells.

LICENCE CONSTRAINT, verified 2026-08-12, and it decides the design: BleachBit is GPL-3.0 and the CleanerML definition files are GPL-3.0+. Vanish is MIT and this repo is public. So:
  - SHIP: a CleanerML parser, written here, MIT. A file format is a specification, not a copyrightable work - implementing a reader for it carries no obligation.
  - DO NOT SHIP: the definition .xml files themselves. Never vendored into this repo.
  - CONSUME: definitions already present on the user's machine (an installed BleachBit's cleaners directory) or a folder the user points at.

That last point is also forced by INV-4 / Rule 6 - the app does not fetch anything over the network, so 'download the latest definitions' is not available to us and must not be designed in.

Caveat recorded honestly: the parser/definitions split is a conservative reading intended to avoid the question entirely rather than win an argument about mere aggregation. Not legal advice; if this ever ships commercially it wants a real review.
design: Order of work: parser + a Vanish-native definition for one category we can verify end to end, THEN the import path for user-supplied CleanerML. Do not start with the import - a parser with no verified execution semantics is untestable.
acceptance_criteria: Each shipped category names its tier in the UI; nothing in NEEDS-ORPHAN-DETECTION removes without its cross-reference; every removal still routes through the vault.
notes:
2026-08-19: SPEC GROUNDED before writing a parser, because guessing a file format is how this codebase produces confident answers about the wrong thing. Read docs.bleachbit.org/cml/cleanerml.html and /cml/variables.html, plus one real Windows definition for its structure only. Nothing was copied into this repo.

ELEMENTS: cleaner[id,os] > label, description, running[type=exe|pathname], var[name] > value, option[id] > label, description, warning, action[...]. Also localizations, which we ignore.

ACTION COMMANDS (18): apt.autoclean, apt.autoremove, chrome.autofill, chrome.databases_db, chrome.favicons, chrome.history, chrome.keywords, delete, ini, json, mozilla_url_history, office_registrymodifications, process, sqlite.vacuum, truncate, win.shell.change.notify, winreg, yum.clean_all.

SEARCH: file (one path), glob (wildcard), walk.files (files under a dir, recursive, no dirs, not the top), walk.all (files AND dirs under it, not the top), walk.top (contents plus the top dir itself), deep (whole-drive scan).

FILTERS: regex / nregex match the BASENAME; wholeregex / nwholeregex match the FULL PATH; n* forms are negations.

OS: bsd, darwin, linux, netbsd, openbsd, unix, windows.

VARIABLES: ~ home; $foo and ${foo} env var, documented case-sensitive; %foo% env var, Windows, case-insensitive; $$foo$$ MULTI-VALUE, one action expanding to several paths ($$ProgramFiles$$ covers both Program Files trees). BleachBit also defines %cd%, %CommonAppData%, %Documents%, %LocalAppData%, %LocalAppDataLow%, %Music%, %Pictures%, %Video%, %ProgramW6432%, %CommonProgramW6432%.

ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION, to be commented in the code: real definitions in the wild write $localappdata in lower case, so a case-SENSITIVE $foo would not resolve on Windows where environment variables are case-insensitive by OS design. Vanish expands both forms case-insensitively.
2026-08-19: BUILT. Host suite 1053/0 (was 973 at session start).

SHIPPED: scanner.ps1 gains the reader (Expand-CleanerMlPath, ConvertFrom-CleanerMlFile, Resolve-CleanerMlAction, Compress-CleanerMlPaths, Find-CleanerMlFindings, Get-CleanerMlDefinitionDirs) plus a read-only cleanerml-probe hook in the same shape as the existing SEC-2/TASK-05 probes. New cleaner id 'definitions'. main.js routes it through the vault. Renderer gets the section, a folder input and a Browse button. New suite test/cleanerml-verify.ps1, 61 assertions, registered in run-all.ps1; 10 more in ui-interaction-full-verify.js for the DOM half.

ONLY 'delete' IS EXECUTED. The other 17 commands edit files in place, drive a package manager or act on the running system, and none is a change the vault can undo. An option containing one is withheld ENTIRELY and named in the panel. 'deep' is refused separately: it is a whole-filesystem scan, not a cleaning rule.

ONE OPTION = ONE ROW = ONE VAULT ENTRY, carrying every path it would move. main.js's purge route now accepts findings.paths as well as findings.path. Paths covered by a parent are pruned first, because the vault takes a directory's children with it and a child listed beside its own parent is a move that cannot happen twice.

NEVER 'Safe'. We did not write these rules. An option with its own <warning> is Advanced and shows the warning.

XXE: a definition file is data, not a program. XmlResolver is null, and the suite plants a canary file plus an external entity pointing at it and asserts the canary never appears in our output.

DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: a Vanish-native definition. The order of work asked for one to prove the pipeline end to end, but every category we could write one for is already covered by a Windows built-in or by the definitions we now read, so it would be the redundant nonsense CLAUDE.md forbids. The end-to-end proof comes from fixture definitions the suite writes itself - parse, expand, match, filter, prune, finding, note - which is stronger than a category we would then have to defend.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, against the issue's own wording: each shipped category names its tier in the UI - YES, findings carry Moderate/Advanced and the renderer shows it. Every removal routes through the vault - YES, kind=file plus paths[]. The NEEDS-ORPHAN-DETECTION clause does not map: it belonged to the hand-written catalogue that was rescoped away. The nearest equivalent that DOES exist is the <running> element, which blocks an option whose application is in use and says which one.

SIDE FIX, and it was pre-existing: renderCleanerBody only rendered state.note when a section found NOTHING, so any cleaner reporting findings AND an explanation lost the explanation in the one case where the user was about to act. uwp-leftovers and profiles were both already losing theirs.

REAL-MACHINE CHECK: engine run on this host returns success with 'No CleanerML definitions were found... will not download them' - no BleachBit installed here, which is the honest empty state rather than an error.
close_reason: Built and tested 2026-08-19. MIT CleanerML reader, the definitions cleaner, the vault route, the folder picker, 61 engine assertions and 10 DOM assertions, host suite 1053/0. No definition file vendored and none shipped - see the issue notes for why a Vanish-native category was deliberately not written. Acceptance against a real BleachBit definitions set is dzr.

title: Settings: reads as a form dump; current elevation state is not stated
description: Operator: 'settings, clean it up, it looks very robotic and the admin/audit toggle isnt very clear. please make its state more persistent and correctly indicative.' The 'Start Vanish as administrator' toggle is about the NEXT start, but it is the only elevation-looking control on the panel, so it reads as the current mode switch. Nothing on the panel says which mode this session is in.
acceptance_criteria: Settings opens with a status block naming the current mode and what it allows, with a way to elevate now when in Audit Mode. The startup toggle says what will happen at the next start, in words, and its state survives a restart.
close_reason: Shipped in 84df077; npm test 338/0, npm run verify 162/0. Elevated confirmation of the three startup writes tracked on vanish-uninstaller-dmu.

title: System Overview cards do not centre; a short last row hugs the left
description: Operator: 'the system overview items need to be center aligned, so whether we have less or more items, they show up in a more aesthetic manner. i dont mean the text, i mean the boxes themselves.' .audit-cards-grid uses repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px,1fr)): auto-fill keeps empty phantom tracks, so a row with fewer cards than columns is left-aligned against dead space.
acceptance_criteria: With any card count and any window width, the grid is centred as a block and no card stretches to an odd width.
close_reason: Shipped in 84df077; npm test 338/0, npm run verify 162/0. Elevated confirmation of the three startup writes tracked on vanish-uninstaller-dmu.

title: System overview: card boxes should stay centred at any item count
description: Operator: 'the system overview items need to be center aligned, so whether we have less or more items, they show up in a more aesthetic manner. i dont mean the text, i mean the boxes themselves.' .audit-cards-grid uses grid auto-fill, so a row that does not fill leaves dead space on the right and the boxes read as left-jammed.

title: Quarantine details: readable but not user-friendly
description:
Operator, 2026-08-06: 'quarantine details are adequate but not user friendly.'

The information is present and correct; the presentation makes the user work for it. Lowest-severity item on the audit list - explicitly acknowledged as adequate - but it is the surface a user visits when anxious about something they just removed, so clarity matters more here than elsewhere.

Needs a design pass rather than a bug fix: what does someone opening this screen actually want to know first (what was removed, from where, can I get it back, what happens if I do nothing), and is that what they see first?
acceptance_criteria: A quarantine entry's screen answers, without the user hunting: what this was, where it came from, when, whether it is restorable, and what happens if left alone. Reviewed against the real vault with real entries.
close_reason: Quarantine entries now answer, without expanding anything: what it was, where it came from, when (relative), whether it is restorable, and - the question the screen never answered - what happens if left alone, read from the live retention setting. Origin translated out of internal route form. The operator's vault is empty (the app was too broken to have quarantined anything), so the harness drives the real renderer with real manifest-shaped entries under both retention settings and says so rather than claiming coverage it lacks.

title: SEC-4 (MEDIUM): commit package-lock.json and pin electron exactly
description:
Found by /cso audit 2026-08-03 (TASK-18). Report: .security-reports/2026-08-03-160528.json finding 4.

package-lock.json is listed in .gitignore (line 2) and is therefore absent from the
repository, while package.json pins electron as ^42.5.0. Nothing in the repo records
which electron build, or which of its install-time transitive dependencies, a given
release was produced from. This is an application repo intended to be published, not
a library, so the lockfile is the artefact that makes a build reproducible and
auditable.

EXPLOIT
1. electron, or any package in its install dependency graph, is compromised at the
   registry (account takeover or malicious version publish).
2. A fresh clone runs npm install. With a caret range and no lockfile, npm resolves
   the newest matching version -- the malicious one -- and runs its install scripts
   with the developer's privileges.
3. The compromise lands in the packaged application, which by design runs elevated
   and deletes files, edits the registry and executes third-party binaries. No
   committed hash exists against which the substitution could be noticed.

FIX
- Remove package-lock.json from .gitignore and commit it (it records integrity hashes).
- Pin electron to an exact version in package.json; bump deliberately.
- Use npm ci rather than npm install for release builds.

npm audit --omit=dev currently reports 0 vulnerabilities, so committing the lockfile
records a clean state rather than an inherited problem.
acceptance_criteria: package-lock.json is tracked in git; electron is pinned to an exact version in package.json; docs/RELEASING.md specifies npm ci for release builds.
close_reason: Fixed in 0a9c880. package-lock.json is now tracked (13 packages, all with integrity hashes, npm audit clean), electron pinned to 42.5.0 exactly, docs/RELEASING.md requires npm ci with the reasoning and adds lockfile + npm audit to the pre-release checklist. Also wired npm test to test/run-all.ps1 - it previously errored out despite the suite existing. VERIFIED: npm ci installs from the committed lockfile and npm test runs the suite at 212 passed / 0 failed.

title: REQ-19 ownership elevator: surface the per-item offer in the UI and verify it
description:
The engine half shipped with TASK-16: Grant-VanishOwnership (takeown /A + icacls granting Administrators full control) runs per item inside Invoke-QuarantineItems, but ONLY when the caller passes allowOwnershipElevation=true AND the transactional move already failed with an access-denied style error. Success is recorded as aclElevated=true on the manifest row.

What is missing:
1. The UI half. FLOW-02's locked-item branch and SCR-06 should offer 'Take ownership and retry' per failed item, not as a blanket toggle - REQ-19 says per item, Full Mode only. main.js already accepts allowOwnershipElevation on purge-remnants and cleaner-purge; nothing in renderer.js sets it yet.
2. Verification. The REQ-19 acceptance ('a TrustedInstaller-owned test file is quarantined after the elevator step') has never been run. It needs a fixture owned by TrustedInstaller, which is awkward to create and clean up safely on a dev machine - do it on the TASK-17 VM.

Until both land, REQ-19 is NOT satisfied and must not be marked complete.
acceptance_criteria: A TrustedInstaller-owned test file fails the first quarantine attempt, the UI offers ownership elevation for that item specifically, accepting it quarantines the file, the manifest row records aclElevated=true, and restore returns the file.
close_reason: REQ-19 UI half done: the purge summary now inspects each failed item and offers 'Take ownership and retry' only on those that failed with an access/permission error, plus 'Find what is holding it' (opens the unlocker) on those that failed because the file was locked. Per item, Full Mode guarded, with an explicit confirm that states the permission change is permanent even after a restore. On success the manifest row carries aclElevated=true and the row updates in place. REMAINING: the acceptance test - quarantining a TrustedInstaller-owned file - still has not run, because creating and cleaning up such a fixture safely on a working machine is risky. It belongs to the TASK-17 VM pass and is called out in the handoff.

title: Driver Store sweeper - manifest-backed removal of orphaned driver packages (Stage 11)
description:
Core ships the driver-store half of REQ-14 as audit-only: cleaner-scan cleaner=drivers lists third-party packages whose published INF is missing from %SystemRoot%\INF, and every finding carries removable=false. Removal is deferred because (a) docs/roadmap.md assigns the Driver Store sweeper to Stage 11, which Rule 16 places in Standard tier, and (b) pnputil /delete-driver destroys the FileRepository copy, so a naive restore manifest would be a promise the vault cannot keep.

Design work needed before implementing: decide what a reversible driver removal actually means. Options: copy oemNN.inf + oemNN.pnf into the vault and re-add with pnputil /add-driver /install on restore (works when the payload was already missing, which is the orphan case); or quarantine the whole FileRepository package folder (needs the REQ-19 ownership elevator for TrustedInstaller-owned files). Whichever is chosen, INV-1 still applies: no removal without a restore path.

Blocked on: Core tier VM-tested (Rule 16).
design: Ghost/Phantom PnP Device Sweep added 2026-08-05, supersedes the earlier narrower 'idle driver' framing (was folded in from Stage 13). Get-PnpDevice Status=Unknown on the operator's machine returned 80 devices: 23 VolumeSnapshot (ghost VSS records, benign), 14 HIDClass + 9 USB + 8 WPD + 4 Keyboard + 2 Mouse + smaller classes (old disconnected peripherals, benign), a handful worth a second look. Same category USBDeview/Device Manager 'show hidden devices' addresses, and driver-store-adjacent -- an unplugged device's superseded driver packages can be exactly what is sitting in this issue's other 5.1GB Driver Store finding. Must comply with new promptgate.md Rule 24 (added 2026-08-05): never show a bare Unknown status -- classify by device class with a plain-language benign/needs-review signal before display. pnputil /remove-device on user-confirmed items only, per-item review (same MANDATORY-REVIEW-GATE pattern as Stage 10/14 tier 3).
acceptance_criteria: A planted orphaned driver package is found, removed, and restored; the restore is verified by pnputil /enum-drivers listing the package again. No removal path exists that lacks a manifest.
notes: PARKED 2026-08-06 alongside the other Standard-tier stages - same reason (epic vanish-uninstaller-7oo takes precedence over new surface). Its own Rule 16 gate was already in force.
close_reason:
Cut as redundant, per operator direction 2026-08-12: 'solve problems that are not solved... dont build redundant nonsense'.

ag0 (Windows Update rollback): Windows Settings > Installed Updates already does this, using the EXACT mechanisms this issue specified - wusa.exe /uninstall and DISM /Remove-Package. Vanish would be a second front-end on the same API with no added capability: the vault cannot make a removed security update reversible in any way Windows' own reinstall does not already, and the issue's own binding requirement (MANDATORY-REVIEW-GATE, no auto tier) means it cannot even be faster. The genuinely unserved question nearby is 'which update correlates with when this machine changed', which is zrw's snapshot diff, not a rollback button.

0ng (Driver Store sweeper): pnputil ships with Windows and Disk Cleanup already offers 'Device driver packages'. Worse, the issue documents that INV-1 CANNOT be honoured here - pnputil /delete-driver destroys the FileRepository copy, so a restore manifest would be a promise the vault cannot keep. Building a removal path that breaks the app's own foundational invariant to duplicate a built-in tool is the definition of what we are cutting. The audit-only half already ships (cleaner-scan cleaner=drivers, removable=false) and is the honest version.

dfe (WMI/DCOM orphans, event log channels, offsets DB): P4, no committed timeline, near-zero user-visible value, and Rule 17 would gate it behind mandatory per-item review anyway. Nothing here is a problem a user has ever reported having.

None of these are deleted work - each is recoverable from bd history if the reasoning changes.
